newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton firm, talk govt to allow more exports.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton firm, talk govt to allow more exports.

text.p: Cotton prices jumped up on the local market as speculation grew that the government may allow more exports, dealer said.
So far in the current year the government has allowed export of 1.22 million bales (170 kg each) and traders were expecting permission to be granted for export of at least 200,000 bales shortly.
Mill buying was slow but stockists were active as new crop arrivals declined .
"Limited arrivals amid limited offerings by the farmers as well as fresh buying by the stockist also helped buoyancy in prices," one dealer said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose 60/85 rupees to 900/975 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose 40 rupees to 1,500/1,675 rupees per maund.
F-414 climbed 30/35 rupees to 1,885/1,900 rupees per maund while Gujarat Kalyan (medium staple) spurted 500/800 rupees to 12,000/12,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
